Note::TexAccessor::line_norm¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::line_norm() const

Canonicalize Line Endings Without Reformatting Source¶

line_norm() converts every CRLF pair (\r\n) and every remaining carriage return (\r) to one line feed (\n). Existing line feeds remain unchanged. It gives downstream scanners one byte-level line convention without changing where lines begin or end.

The operation is deliberately narrower than fix_linebreaks. It does not remove trailing spaces, cap blank-line runs, trim the document, or interpret TeX commands. It is also distinct from dedup_blank_lines, which controls the number of empty lines while preserving their existing line-ending spelling. Compose the two when both canonical LF bytes and bounded vertical whitespace are required.

Normalization is lane-wise and shape preserving. Empty cells stay empty; a terminal CR becomes a terminal LF; a CRLF pair becomes exactly one LF rather than two. Applying the method again cannot change the result. The receiver is unchanged and the returned Text Note owns a new packed arena with the same rank and shape.

Undefined input remains undefined. Defined Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes Notes are rejected: line-ending semantics belong to validated Text, not opaque bytes. Runtime and output allocation are linear in the source byte count; no per-line container is constructed.

Example 1: Normalize Every Input Convention In A Matrix¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a\r\nb\rc\n", "stable", "", "x\r"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto normalized = source.tex().line_norm();

std::cout << normalized << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a\nb\nc\n", "stable"],
  ["", "x\n"]
]

CRLF is consumed as one unit, lone CR is replaced, existing LF is retained, and the terminal line boundary remains terminal.

Example 2: Verify Shape And Idempotence¶

const auto twice = normalized.tex().line_norm();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "same_shape=" << (twice.sizes() == source.sizes())
          << " idempotent=" << (twice == normalized).all().bool_item()
          << '\n';

Output¶

same_shape=true idempotent=true

Example 3: Compose With Blank-Line Deduplication¶

const auto compact =
    pluss::make_note("one\r\n \r\n\t\r\ntwo")
        .tex().line_norm().tex().dedup_blank_lines();
std::cout << compact << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"one\n\ntwo"

Order matters: normalization establishes LF first, then blank-line reduction removes whitespace from the collapsed empty run.

Example 4: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().line_norm().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().line_norm();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "line norm Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
line norm Int64: rejected
